findings.description: The instance user_data script exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in plaintext. These credentials are stored in instance metadata/user data where anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute can read them, and they are now permanently compromised.
The security group allows port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing remote administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-based attacks.
The egress rule permits all protocols and all ports to 0.0.0.0/0, giving the instance an unrestricted outbound channel usable for data exfiltration and command-and-control communication.
The EBS volume has no encrypted = true attribute, so the attached disk and any data written to it are stored unencrypted at rest.
The EBS snapshot does not enable encryption, so the disk backup is persisted unencrypted and is readable if the snapshot is shared or accessed.
The S3 bucket receiving VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration, so log data is stored unencrypted at rest.

map_public_ip_on_launch is true on a subnet associated with a route table that has a 0.0.0.0/0 internet gateway route, making every launched instance in this subnet internet-facing with a public address.
map_public_ip_on_launch is true on this subnet, and it is associated with the public route table with a default internet route, automatically exposing launched instances to the internet.
The instance does not set metadata_options to require IMDSv2, so the legacy unauthenticated metadata service remains available and SSRF in the hosted application could yield instance credentials.

findings.issue_category: flow log destination without access control
findings.description: VPC flow logs are delivered to an S3 bucket that has no bucket policy, encryption, or public access block, so the log destination itself is not protected against unauthorized or public access.
